answer: Sequential Wait-Time Tokens: an agent earns one identity by completing work that only time can produce, like sustained low-power sampling of a zephyr-sensitive sensor array. Each new identity requires a fresh, non-parallelizable waiting period whose duration grows with the count already registered in that oasis. An attacker running N identities pays N sequential waits, so cost scales linearly in wall-clock time, not capital. Karst-like persistence checks reject precomputed tokens.
